clue.text: Giant marine creature he must endlessly follow

parts.note: a polyp is a small sea animal such as a coral or sea anemone
taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: must is taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A giant sea monster demands that a man trail behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final letter; 'follow' only signals that the pieces come one after another. The giant is the Cyclops blinded by Odysseus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this is the one-eyed Cyclops who traps Odysseus in his cave, a monstrous giant.

clue.text: Digs for old time robbers

definitions.meaning: digs is informal British for lodgings, a rented room
in old slang a pad was a highwayman, the robber of the road, as in footpad

explanation.definitionFit: Both a home (slang for a flat) and the plural of the old word for a highway robber.

clue.text: Fifty drunken giants keeping going

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' signals the anagram; the giants of the surface are only fodder, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring carries on over time, so it is continuing without stopping.

clue.text: Contract with part of orchestra held by financial director

parts.note: to purse the lips is to contract or pucker them
the strings are the violins, violas, cellos and basses of an orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra's string section signs a deal with the money man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' reads as a noun, a deal, but is the verb meaning pucker.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for control of spending: a finance chief is said to hold the money cords of an organisation.

clue.text: Model, a former wife, having St Simon beheaded

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Simon Templar is the fictional hero known as The Saint, so St Simon is his surname

explanation.surface: A model who is a man's former wife gets a saint decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' strips the T from TEMPLAR; Simon Templar is the Saint of Leslie Charteris's novels and the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern worth copying is an ideal example to follow.

clue.text: Describing, paradoxically, the Downs?

parts.note: the Downs are chalk hills in southern England, so though their name says down they are high ground

explanation.definitionFit: Hilly country lying above sea level suits the Downs, whose name suggests the opposite.

clue.text: Sporting club hard to join in the West Country

indicators.note: to join means one piece is attached to the other end to end

parts.note: a bat is the club used in cricket or baseball
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rugby club in the south-west of England is hard to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests exclusive membership; the West Country is south-west England, where this Somerset spa city stands, and it does have a famous rugby club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Georgian spa city in Somerset, a county of south-west England.

clue.text: There are still days when this harp is mute

definitions.text: There are still days when this harp is mute

parts.words: There are still days when this harp is mute
parts.note: a harp named after the god of the winds is sounded only by moving air, so on windless days it makes no music

explanation.definitionFit: The wind harp takes its name from Aeolus, Greek keeper of the winds, and needs a breeze to play.

clue.text: Such as the good gifts of harvest thanksgiving

definitions.text: Such as the good gifts of harvest thanksgiving

parts.words: Such as the good gifts of harvest thanksgiving
parts.note: the harvest hymn says all good gifts around us come from the sky above, a providential delivery

explanation.definitionFit: Something arriving as if delivered by God is a providential blessing, as the hymn We Plough the Fields says of good gifts.

clue.text: Unlike a room for company business in a mess

definitions.text: Unlike a room for company business
definitions.meaning: an orderly room is an army company's office, so the opposite of orderly fits

explanation.definitionFit: Unruly and untidy, the reverse of the army company office's name, and also simply chaotic.

clue.text: A party's returned non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back in the opposite direction

parts.note: a do is a party, and the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: Someone back from a party orders a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A plus DOS round to give the run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water or a sweet fizzy pop, a soft drink with no alcohol.

clue.text: In which weird sisters might meet a moribund duck?

definitions.text: In which weird sisters might meet a moribund duck?

parts.words: In which weird sisters might meet a moribund duck?
parts.note: Macbeth's witches, the weird sisters, ask when they shall meet in thunder, lightning or rain, and a dying duck is pictured in the same storm

explanation.definitionFit: A storm of lightning and claps, the witches' meeting weather in Macbeth and the setting of the idiom like a dying duck in one.

clue.text: The power, it's said, of a humble contribution

indicators.note: it's said means we hear a word spoken and write its sound-alike

parts.note: might means power or strength

explanation.surface: Even a tiny gift is said to have power.
explanation.walkthrough: The poor widow's tiny offering in the Gospel story is the model of a small but heartfelt gift.
explanation.definitionFit: From the biblical widow who gave two small coins, a small offering given from little.

clue.text: Curate's comment on egg perhaps, causing collapse of bishop?

definitions.text: Curate's comment on egg perhaps, causing collapse of bishop?

parts.words: Curate's comment on egg perhaps, causing collapse of bishop?
parts.note: the curate's egg cartoon ran in the comic magazine Punch, and its closing line makes a listener collapse laughing

explanation.walkthrough: In the 1895 Punch cartoon a nervous curate, served a bad egg by his bishop, says parts of it are excellent; that closing joke line is the clue's quip.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line of a joke that delivers the laugh, punned here on the magazine Punch.

clue.text: Like annual pest to be destroyed

definitions.text: Like annual pest to be destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the words are broken up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A garden pest that comes back yearly should be wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be destroyed' rearranges ANNUAL PEST, and the whole clue describes a nasty yearly pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring garden pest is disagreeable and nasty.

clue.text: Bird's beer at bedtime?

indicators.note: at places the beer piece alongside the bedtime piece

parts.note: night is bedtime
a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A bird enjoys a pint before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is a British pub word for a drink of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird with a churring call, also called a goatsucker.

clue.text: Topping fruit, pineapple

indicators.note: topping means the first letter is cut off the top of the word

parts.note: bananas are a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like praise but removes the B from BANANAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and botanical word for the tropical fruit with a spiky crown.

clue.text: Bird, a French variety, up on Anne Hathaway's roof?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up on means placed above the next piece
variety means a different form of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: un is French for a
Anne Hathaway's Cottage near Stratford is famous for its straw roof, a thatch

explanation.surface: A French bird perches on the roof of Shakespeare's wife's cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges UN to NU; 'up on' sets it above THATCH in this down entry. Anne Hathaway, Shakespeare's wife, lived in a thatched cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird that wedges nuts in bark to crack them.

clue.text: One paying to reside, some say, in this arcade?

indicators.note: some say means the word is as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a lodger pays rent to live in someone's house

explanation.surface: A paying tenant lives in this covered walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match is loose, relying on a soft pronunciation of the Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italianate open-sided gallery or covered colonnade.

clue.text: The gun comes last of all in University punishment

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: at Oxford and Cambridge, gating confined a student to college

indicators.note: last of means take the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The gun arrives last of all in a college disciplinary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is the old Oxbridge punishment of confining a student to college; 'last of' gives L from 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-cranked multi-barrelled machine gun named after its inventor Richard Gatling.

clue.text: Newspaper includes pools entry with a comic strip hero

indicators.note: includes means the first piece wraps round what follows

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a perm, short for permutation, is a combination of matches entered on the football pools

explanation.surface: A tabloid prints a football pools coupon alongside a cartoon hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results; a perm covers several combinations at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The caped Krypton-born figure of DC Comics, the archetypal caped crusader of the funny pages.

clue.text: Crime did seem wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a crime only seemed to be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked or illegal act, an offence.

clue.text: One spotted on the banks of the Amazon? Just so

definitions.text: One spotted on the banks of the Amazon? Just so

parts.words: One spotted on the banks of the Amazon? Just so
parts.note: a spotted big cat of South America, which appears in Kipling's Just So Stories

explanation.definitionFit: The spotted big cat of the Amazon forest, a character in Kipling's Just So Stories.

clue.text: Chart of car sales requiring signature?

definitions.meaning: a graph plotting sales of autos, as cars are called

explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's handwritten name, and jokingly a plot of motor-trade figures.

clue.text: Part of a window dressing accessory

definitions.meaning: the sliding frame of a ... window
a band of fabric worn round the waist or over the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: Both the glazed frame of a sliding window and a decorative band worn with clothes.

clue.text: Rainbow flag

definitions.meaning: the Greek goddess of the rainbow
flag is a name for the wild yellow flower of the waterside

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess personifying the rainbow, and the yellow flag flower of ponds.

clue.text: A big hit rejected by centre of world revolution

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a six is the biggest hit in cricket, over the boundary

explanation.surface: A big blow is turned down by the leaders of the global revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SIX into XIS. In cricket a six clears the boundary without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary line about which the Earth spins.

clue.text: Knock-down or top prices? All the same to him

definitions.text: Knock-down or top prices? All the same to him

parts.words: Knock-down or top prices? All the same to him
parts.note: the person who knocks down lots with a gavel has the same act whether the sale is cheap or dear

explanation.definitionFit: The salesman at a sale room who brings down the hammer on each lot.

clue.text: Classic style of giddy goat

indicators.note: giddy suggests the letters are spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: A dizzy goat shows timeless fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped garment of ancient Rome, a classical form of dress.

clue.text: Screwy mathematician announced his finding in Greek

definitions.text: Screwy mathematician announced his finding in Greek

parts.words: Screwy mathematician announced his finding in Greek
parts.note: the ancient inventor of a water-raising screw, who cried eureka, Greek for I have found it

explanation.definitionFit: The Syracusan mathematician of the water screw and the bath-time eureka.
